title: Sangat online
hookLine: online kirtan and study groups can help, with care
tomorrow: why would Guru Nanak bless a rude village to stay right where it was?
last: A WEEK OF SEVA AND SANGAT.

cards: Sunday night, ten o'clock. Jas sends a link: a video kirtan with her Friday group and a few cousins from three time zones. Simran joins from her bed with the lights off.
Eight little squares, one person on a tabla, someone's cat walking across a keyboard. Then her phone buzzes. A meme.
Then another. By the second shabad she realizes she's been in two group chats and zero kirtan.

teach.h: ANG 72 DOESN'T ASK FOR A ROOM.
teach.b: So does a screen count? Go back to the test from this week, Ang 72: the true company is known where the one Name is spoken. That test doesn't ask for a room.
Eight squares singing the same shabad can pass it.

teach.h: A LIFELINE FOR THE FAR AND THE SICK.
teach.b: For someone two hours from a gurdwara, or too sick to leave the house, an online kirtan or study circle can be a real lifeline.
But the test does ask for the Name to be heard, and a screen is built to pull you somewhere else.
So some Sikhs who keep sangat online set a few guards. Notifications off. Camera on if the group wants it, a scarf or a covered head as you would in the hall.

And the screen doesn't replace everything: nobody can serve langar through a video call, or wipe a stranger's shoes. Simran turns her phone face down, joins the next line out loud, and Jas sees her lips moving and grins.

how: Some gurdwaras stream the Hukamnama and kirtan, and Sikhs join online Sukhmani, Nitnem and study circles, alongside an in-person sangat when they can reach one.

games.q: you're in a video kirtan and a friend messages you. what fits today?
o: phone face down, one tab open, and sing the next line.
reply quickly; it still counts because the kirtan is playing.
leave the call; online sangat doesn't count anyway.
games.why: the test is whether the Name is heard. a screen can pass it, if you give it the attention a room would get.

practice: A gratitude count. On one hand, count the people who were sangat for you this past week, in a room or on a screen, one finger for each, and say each name silently as you fold it down.
If you run out of names, keep the hand open and wait.

wordCard.voice: Sangat online. Company where the Name is spoken, through a screen, kept with care: one tab, phone down.

carryVoice: This one goes with you: sangat anywhere, as long as the Name can be heard there. A week done.

sources.ref: Ang 72, Sri Raag, Guru Nanak (satsangat kaisee jaaneeai, jithai eko naam vakhaaneeai), paraphrased
